findings.body: In `public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts` at line 281, the function `groupHasPendingRequests` mutates the `cycle` property of the group by setting it to `nextCycle`. This side effect during a predicate check is unexpected and can cause incorrect behavior in the iteration logic that depends on `cycle`. Predicate functions should not mutate their inputs as it can lead to subtle bugs and make the code harder to reason about.
findings.suggestion: Refactor `groupHasPendingRequests` to avoid mutating `group.cycle`. Instead, update `cycle` explicitly in the calling code after confirming the group has pending requests.
findings.title: Predicate function `groupHasPendingRequests` mutates input group state

findings.body: In the tests added in `public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.test.ts` and `public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.test.ts`, the interpolation of template variables is verified. However, there is no test verifying behavior when `applyTemplateVariables` throws an error or returns invalid queries. This could lead to unhandled exceptions or unexpected behavior in production.
findings.suggestion: Add tests to verify that `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery` handle errors thrown by `applyTemplateVariables` gracefully.
findings.title: Missing tests for error handling in template variable interpolation

findings.body: In `public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts` at line 296, the `runSplitQuery` function now applies template variable interpolation to queries before splitting and running them. This is a positive change and aligns with the tests added to verify interpolation. However, the change assumes that `datasource.applyTemplateVariables` is synchronous and side-effect free. If `applyTemplateVariables` has side effects or asynchronous behavior, this could cause issues. The tests mock this method as synchronous, so this is likely safe, but it is worth confirming the contract of `applyTemplateVariables`.
findings.suggestion: Confirm that `applyTemplateVariables` is synchronous and side-effect free. If not, consider handling asynchronous interpolation properly.
findings.title: Assumption that `applyTemplateVariables` is synchronous in `runSplitQuery`

findings.body: In `public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts` at line 163, `runSplitQuery` is called with options `{ skipPartialUpdates: true, disableRetry: true }`. This disables retry logic for shard split queries, which may reduce robustness against transient errors. The retry logic is handled separately in `runShardSplitQuery`. This is likely intentional, but it should be documented clearly to avoid confusion.
findings.suggestion: Add a comment explaining why retries are disabled when calling `runSplitQuery` from `runShardSplitQuery`.
findings.title: Retries disabled in nested `runSplitQuery` call in shard splitting

models.summary: The change adds template variable interpolation before query splitting in both `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery`, improving correctness and test coverage. However, a critical bug is present in `groupHasPendingRequests` where it mutates input state unexpectedly, which can cause incorrect query splitting behavior. Some minor correctness and documentation improvements are suggested, along with additional tests for error handling.
